text:
deploy-bot: :new: deploy v3.14-canary started -> canary-id=canary-213567, routing 3% traffic to us-west-2 and eu-west-1

Tomas: seeing a 12% spike in 5xxs from the canary shards in eu-west-1, started ~2m after rollout. errors look like timeouts to encoder service. logs attached below. :rotating_light:

sarah: ack. i'm pausing traffic routing for the canary and triggering automated rollback. will post commands.

deploy-bot: Automated rollback initiated for canary-213567. Rolling back to stable v3.13. Attempting region-by-region rollback.

Irene: i'm still seeing ~200 connections on the canary pods in eu-west-1: they aren't draining cleanly. DB migration may have left sessions sticky.

mike: that matches what i see in cloud-sql: a long-running prepared-statement lock from the migration job started at 09:12 UTC. might block pod termination.

Tomas: paste of error trace from encoder pods:
```
2026-03-15T09:14:03Z ERROR encoder.cpp:142 handle_request failed: rpc_timeout (elapsed 12.1s)
  at encoder::process_request(encoder.cpp:98)
  at net::connection::dispatch(net.cpp:67)
```

sarah: automated rollback succeeded in us-west-2 (2% -> 0%). eu-west-1 rollback failed to lower canary routing; looks like the router still has active endpoints.

Irene: can we flip the feature flag to short-circuit the new encoder path? flag name is use_new_encoder. If we set it to false we should avoid the stuck code path while we drain pods.

sarah: good call. i'm running the flag command now:
```
rdctl flag set use_new_encoder=false --env=prod --reason "emergency: canary encoder timeouts" --actor sarah
```

sarah: flag is set. please verify traffic now.

Tomas: running quick smoke against edge: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "x-api-key:REDACTED" https://api.redwood.internal/encode -d '{"text":"hello"}'`

Tomas: results: us-west-2 --> 200 0.18s, eu-west-1 --> 200 0.21s (some hosts still 504/0.9s).

mike: the DB lock: found the migration job (job id mj-889) holding a session. i'm going to kill the session after checking with infra; that should free connections and allow pods to drain.

Irene: before killing, which customers impacted? ops dashboard shows a 0.28% increase in 5xxs overall, but two higher-tier tenants (AcmeCorp and Meridian) are seeing increased latency and occasional 504s. Customer-success pinged Acme already.

sarah: paging product oncall for customer impact- assessment. @pager-duty please escalate to CS.

pager-duty: paging cs-team: incident 2135678901 -> AcmeCorp latency/504s, assigned to @cs-oncall. Notification sent.

mike: session killed, confirmed migration job terminated. DB locks cleared. starting graceful drain on canary pods in eu-west-1:
```
kubectl -n prod label pod canary-213567-drain=true
kubectl -n prod drain pod/canary-213567-a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
kubectl -n prod drain pod/canary-213567-b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

Tomas: pods draining. router health checks now show less capacity on canary endpoints. manual rollback command to force routing prune:
```
rdctl rollback --canary-id=canary-213567 --force --regions=eu-west-1
```

deploy-bot: Manual rollback acknowledged. Removing canary endpoints from router in eu-west-1.

Irene: monitoring logs and traces. running a sampling query for recent 5xxs to ensure no latent errors:
```
query: service:encoder status:5xx since:10m | group_by(host) | count()
```

Tomas: sampling shows counts dropping to baseline within 3 minutes. last 5xx from canary host 10.10.7.89 at 09:28 UTC.

sarah: status update for incident channel: traffic pulled off canary in both regions. feature flag rolled back. database locks cleared. observed customer impact: small percentage of requests 504/timeout, impacting two enterprise tenants for ~16 minutes. No data loss.

Irene: handing off to europe oncall for verification and postmortem lead. i'll be wrapping the pager-handoff now — @irene is the primary for follow-up.

Irene: taking ownership for postmortem. action items: 1) why migration job ran during canary, 2) why automated rollback didn't prune eu-west routing, 3) improve kill-switch documentation and script.

mike: i'll open a db-ticket to gate migrations during canary windows and add a check to the migration runner to detect active canaries.

Tomas: next immediate verification steps: run canary smoke suite, check trace sampling for error-rate regression, validate no lingering DB sessions, and confirm customer mitigations with CS.

sarah: agreed. i'll keep monitoring for 30m and then move to resolved if green. please add any notes to the incident doc in confluence: /incidents/2135678901-evacuate-canary-partial-fallback

deploy-bot: Incident state -> mitigation_in_progress. Events logged.

Irene: noted. i'll start the postmortem doc and tag owners. thanks everyone for quick coordination. :white_check_mark:
